name: design-skill-evals
job: Design a falsifiable Skill Evaluation Program that can disprove whether an exact skill bundle improves realistic work.

inScope: Freezing the falsifiable question and exact candidate identities/digests
Designing full-catalog auto-injection datasets (positives, near-neighbours, abstentions, compound, multilingual)
Designing unseen behavior tasks with deterministic assertions and critical-failure modes
Building the control matrix (base, expert, skill, comparator) and answer/judge/provider matrix
Specifying holdouts, protected raw-artifact stores, commitments, receipts, replay, expiry
Defining metrics, uncertainty, cost/latency, failure triage and regression fixtures
outOfScope: Running evals at production scale or owning live outcome telemetry (host/Control Plane)
Treating self-attested green scores as proof without replay

inputs: The exact skill bundle (name, description, body, references, scripts)
Intended jobs, artifacts, nearest neighbours and risks
Supported runtimes/tools, output budget and the claim the eval may falsify
Eval store policy for raw artifacts, audience, access, retention
outputs: One Skill Evaluation Program with the seven-part output contract
Protected holdout and raw-artifact store with commitment and disclosure rule
Qualification-record evidence filed when the run is completed

data: protected eval store for raw artifacts and holdouts
permissions: declared eval-store access, audience, retention and deletion policy

failureSemantics: A green score is invalid without exact candidate binding, complete artifacts, independent recomputation, provenance and replay; failures become minimal regression cases and the skill is edited, never the threshold; any relevant byte change invalidates the matching proof.

outcome.observable: An independent runner can reproduce the candidate, tasks, outputs, metrics and verdict without trusting the author narrative, and the result is recorded as version-scoped qualification evidence.
